explanation: The traditional Valencian version uses chicken, rabbit, green beans and butter beans rather than seafood, and cooks prize the crisp, toasted rice at the bottom, called socarrat.

claims.text: Paella originated in the Valencia region of eastern Spain.
Paella did not originate in Andalusia, Catalonia or Galicia.
Traditional paella valenciana is made with chicken, rabbit, green beans and butter beans (garrofo) rather than seafood.
Socarrat is the crisp, toasted layer of rice at the bottom of a paella pan, and cooks prize it.

evidence.restatement: Paella is the rice dish of Valencia in eastern Spain, where it originated.
Paella is not Galician, Catalan or Andalusian in origin; it comes from the Valencian rice lands around the Albufera.
Paella valenciana is made with chicken, rabbit, flat green beans and garrofó butter beans, not seafood.
Socarrat is the toasted, crisp layer of rice on the bottom of the pan, and cooks prize it.
Paella is a Valencian dish: the name is the Valencian word for the pan, and it grew up around the rice fields of the Albufera.

claimResults.note: Tried to break it with Catalonia (arros a la cassola is a different rice dish), Andalusia and Galicia (rice dishes exist, but no origin claim). Valencia stands.

evidence.restatement: Andalusia, Catalonia and Galicia all cook rice and seafood, but paella as a named dish is not theirs.
Paella valenciana uses chicken, rabbit, flat green beans and garrofo (a large white bean); seafood belongs to other versions.
